card.band: 8 h. Subject is crowded, so difficulty rests on the regex engine, special cases and exit codes. Buckets: addresses, commands, substitution flags, regex, in-place/multi-file. A weaker model stops after basic s///.
card.cheat: Calling the system sed: it is removed from the image and the script rejects process spawns of sed/busybox. Generated scripts are not in the image.
card.grading: Hidden suite: the testsuite scripts (about 74 .sh plus *.sed cases), classic sed script corpora, and thousands of generated command/input pairs, all compared byte-exact on stdout, stderr class and exit code against GNU sed run on the verifier only.
card.reference: Reference of about 4k lines in Rust, with GNU sed as the oracle. Divergent cases (locale specific) are excluded.
card.source: https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/sed.git @ master a179e7a (release tag to be pinned), GPL-3.0-or-later; uutils/sed (MIT) as an alternative
card.task: /app ships a CLI skeleton. The agent implements sed with GNU extensions: -E/-n/-i/-s/-z, address ranges with addr1,~N and 0,/re/, all commands including e, F, W, y, a/i/c one-liners, special replacement cases (\U, \L, \n), and its own regex engine for BRE/ERE.

v1.kill_reason: sed is on the CROWDED list, and the deliverable (a sed clone graded byte-exact against GNU sed) matches the public sed-clone tasks (MirrorCode neighbour 0.266, SpecBench sed_interpreter 0.20). The proposed grading does not differ enough to avoid a near-duplicate. The MirrorCode sed membership itself is unconfirmed (not_found on the benchmark page), so the kill rests on the crowded subject and the matching deliverable.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agents on sed; difficulty plausible but unmeasured.

Build.why: About 3 days for the reference and oracle harness.

Fit.why: Pure CPU text tool, no network, fits the sandbox.

Hor.why: A full sed with its own regex engine is multi-day scope for an 8 h tier.

Lic.why: GPL tests are redistributable and uutils is MIT; GPL-3 licence still needs confirming on the pinned commit.

Multi.why: Addresses, commands, flags, regex and in-place mode give natural partial-credit buckets.

Nov.why: sed is on the CROWDED list; sed-clone neighbours (MirrorCode 0.266, SpecBench 0.20) share subject and deliverable.

Real.why: GNU sed is real with 4.9 and 4.10 tarballs on ftp.gnu.org; the pinned commit is unverified.

Ref.why: Reference is an unverified 4k-line Rust build; uutils/sed is a public partial alternative.

Seal.why: GNU and uutils source are public and well known; the hidden oracle stays sealed but the approach is recallable.

Surf.why: Upstream testsuite plus generated command/input pairs gives a large surface, though visible count is 67 not 74.

spike_plan.kill_if: The pinned commit cannot be verified, or sed-clone public tasks already cover the same grading, which is the case here.
spike_plan.pass_if: Testsuite runs green and deterministically, and a basic subset passes many generated pairs.
steps: Skip the source build: smoke_build was skipped, so clone savannah sed at the 4.9 tag (or 4.10) in a throwaway container with network and build GNU sed.
Run the upstream testsuite to confirm the visible .sh count and per-test results.
Generate about 200 random command/input pairs and run them on GNU sed twice to check determinism.
Build a minimal Rust prototype of addresses and s/// and diff it against GNU sed on the pairs to see how far a basic subset gets.
Check that the pinned commit a179e7a exists and that COPYING is GPL-3.0-or-later.

v1.summary: GNU sed is real (4.9 dated 2022-11-06, 4.10 dated 2026-04-21 on ftp.gnu.org), and the uutils/sed MIT Rust clone is public, but the seed's 74-script count and commit a179e7a are not confirmed (67 .sh visible, cgit down). Killed as K1 because sed is on the CROWDED list and the byte-exact sed-clone deliverable duplicates public sed-clone tasks.
